title: Ghost Ball Aiming in Pool: A Beginner's Guide to Making More Shots
description: Learn the ghost ball aiming method step by step, avoid the most common beginner mistakes and use a 10-minute drill to start making more cut shots.
body:
Every pool player has had that moment: the shot looks easy, the stroke feels smooth, and the ball rattles off the point of the pocket anyway. The good news is that aiming is a skill you can learn, and one of the most popular beginner methods comes with a spooky name: the ghost ball.

What is the ghost ball?

The ghost ball is an imaginary cue ball sitting right against the object ball at the exact spot where the real cue ball must be at the moment of contact. If the cue ball arrives there, the object ball gets sent along the line toward the pocket.

It sounds fancy, but the big idea is simple: you are not aiming at the object ball. You are aiming at the ghost. Many beginners aim straight at the object ball itself, which is why they miss thin cuts and thick cuts again and again.

Step by step: find the ghost

  1. Find the pocket line. Picture a straight line from the center of the pocket through the center of the object ball and keep going backward, behind the ball.
  2. Place the ghost. On that line, imagine a second ball touching the back of the object ball. Its center is exactly one ball width (about 2 1/4 inches) behind the object ball's center.
  3. Aim at the ghost's center. Walk behind the cue ball and line the cue ball's center up with the center of the ghost.
  4. Get down on that line. Keep your eyes on the target as you settle into your stance, then pause and stroke through smoothly.

If your stance wobbles, our bridge and stance guide will help you stay locked on the line you just found.

Why it works for every angle

On a straight-in shot, the ghost ball sits directly behind the object ball, so you simply hit it full. On a gentle cut, the ghost sits a little off to one side. On a thin cut, it sits almost fully off to the side, so you only brush the edge of the object ball. The method scales smoothly, which is why coaches love it for new players.

  • Straight shot: ghost directly behind the object ball, a full-ball hit.
  • Half-ball cut: ghost centered about half a ball off the object ball's center line.
  • Thin cut: ghost far to the side, just a sliver of contact.

Common mistakes

Aiming at the object ball

This is the number one habit to break. Keep reminding yourself that the ghost is the target.

Forgetting the cue ball's width

The cue ball has size, so the line from your cue tip to the cue ball's center matters more than where the cue tip points on the cloth. Line up the center of the cue ball, not the edge.

Blaming your aim when it is your stroke

Plenty of missed shots come from a stroke that swerves at the last second. If you are aiming well but still missing, slow down and check that your cue travels in a straight line. The spin habits in our cue ball spin guide can also push the object ball slightly off line, so start with a center-ball hit while you learn.

A simple 10-minute practice plan

  1. Place an object ball near a corner pocket and the cue ball in line with it. Make 5 straight-in shots in a row.
  2. Move the cue ball a few inches to one side to create a gentle cut. Picture the ghost before every shot. Make 5.
  3. Try the same cut from the other side. Left and right cuts feel different, so practice both.
  4. Add a medium cut, then a thin one. Move on only when you are making about 7 out of 10.

Want a quick way to train your eye? Try the free aim trainer on this site, then take your new skill to a real table. You can find a place to play on our tournaments page or check the pool calendar to watch how the pros handle cut shots live.

Is ghost ball the only method?

No. Players also use fractional aiming, the contact-point approach and various systems that are based on the diamonds on the rails. Many strong players mix methods, and a lot of shot making ends up being feel built from thousands of repetitions. But the ghost ball is a friendly place to start because it gives your brain a clear picture to aim at.

Take it to the table

This week, spend ten minutes on each practice session just on cut shots. Before every shot, say to yourself: where is the ghost? In a short time, you will start to see it without thinking, the same way a pro does when lining up a tough cut in the Mosconi Cup, coming to Orlando November 27-30. See what is coming up on our Mosconi Cup 2026 hub.

So, how about you: do you aim at the ghost, at the contact point, or just trust your feel?
